chunk_findings.detail: `_regression_status` ends with `return "could-not-run", {**ev, "reason": f"unrecognized verification status {status!r}"}`. This path produces the same `"could-not-run"` status the CLI now special-cases, so `could_not_run_text` is invoked on an `ev` that has no `"remedy"` key (unlike the two `_verify_regression` early returns and unlike the `G.REGRESSION_COULD_NOT_RUN` branch, which sets `_REMEDY`). Given e.g. a gates status string that is not one of the constants (`G.verify_regression_test` returns `"skipped-dirty-tree"` or any future constant), the record carries `regression_verified == "could-not-run"` and `regression_verify == {"reason": "unrecognized verification status 'skipped-dirty-tree'"}`; `could_not_run_text` then returns just that reason with no `" -- to fix: ..."` suffix, so the user is told why it did not run but not what would let it run — the exact half of the fix's stated contract ("Never silent: every could-not-run names its reason, and what would let it run") that this branch omits. Reusing `ev.get("remedy") or _REMEDY` in the fallback (or routing it through the same branch) would make the contract hold for every status.

chunk_findings.detail: `tree_provides` reports "the test is not in the base's test files" for every non-`passed` outcome of the collection probe, not just for a genuinely absent test. Concretely: base tree contains `tests/test_widget.py` with `def test_widget` (so the old check returned True and the tests were actually run at base), but the module does `import <something>` that fails to collect at the base commit — e.g. the fix adds/renames a symbol the test imports at module level, or a test-only dependency (`pytest-asyncio`, `httpx`, …) is not installed in the environment running ddflow. pytest then exits 2/4 with a collection error, `run_command_gate` yields a non-`passed` outcome, `tree_provides` returns False, and `verify_test_only_fix` sets `restored = "not run (the test is not in the base's test files)"`. That message is false (the base file plainly defines the test, as the deleted `_exists_at_base` proved) and the restored-test-files check is skipped again, so for any test pytest cannot *collect* the gate silently degrades to the mutation-only path — the bug this change claims to close. The pre-check's `is_file()` test only rules out the missing-file case; it cannot distinguish "absent" from "collect failed". The same conflation happens on exit code 5 (zero items collected, e.g. a spec that is a bare file path or a test parametrized to zero cases): the base file exists but `outcome == "passed"` is False. No `_ev`/reason is inspected, so this is indistinguishable from real absence at the call site.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_collect.py:32-35 (return outcome == "passed")

chunk_findings.detail: The added test never drives the path the bug report and the change's own intent describe. Its own comment admits the reason: "The gate itself, not `bug fixed`: its static name check (`_unresolved_tests`) does not see a re-export either, a separate defect filed on its own." So it deliberately calls the internal service function `G.verify_regression_test(repo, Config.load(repo), tree=wt, base="main", tests=["tests/test_v.py::test_v"])` with the node id already resolved, side-stepping the CLI/gate name-resolution step. Concrete repro: in the exact repository this test builds, a user closes the bug with the documented command, `ddflow bug fixed B1 --regression-test tests/test_v.py::test_v` (or `ddflow complete fix-B1 --regression-test ...`), and the gate reaches `_unresolved_tests` first. Per the test's own comment that check also fails to see a name that is only imported/re-exported, so the re-exported-test scenario is still rejected in the user-facing flow — i.e. the reported bug (the restored-test-files verification being skipped for re-exported tests) is not reproducible-then-fixed through the actual workflow; only one internal helper is. The change therefore does not satisfy the hard ddflow requirement that the bug-closing change carry a regression test that reproduces the reported bug through the workflow it belongs to [D-rules-hierarchy]. Making the test call the CLI (or extending the fix so `_unresolved_tests` also resolves collected node ids) is what would demonstrate the bug as reported is actually gone.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_regression_testfix.py:242 (test_a_test_the_base_re_exports_is_seen_as_existing_there)

chunk_findings.detail: `tree_provides` collapses every non-zero pytest exit status into "the named test is not present in the base tree" (`return outcome == "passed"`, line 33), but pytest distinguishes *node id not found* (exit 4) from a *collection error in the target file* (exit 2, e.g. ImportError/SyntaxError raised while importing the module or its `conftest.py`, missing plugin, etc.). The replacement of `_exists_at_base` therefore changes the answer for inputs the old text scan handled correctly. Concrete input: at base, `tests/test_api.py` contains a top-level `from mymod import new_helper` (the symbol the fix adds) and `def test_new_helper(): ...`. The old `_exists_at_base` read the file and matched the literal `def test_new_helper`, returning True, so the restored-test-files check ran and observed the base failure. With this change, `pytest --collect-only -q` aborts with a collection error and exit code 2, `tree_provides` returns False, and `verify_test_only_fix` records `restored = "not run (the test is not in the base's test files)"` — the very silent skip that bug B9f3ae012b9 is about, for exactly the class of regression tests that import the fixed API at module scope. The same applies to any configured command that is not pytest (the code unconditionally appends `--collect-only -q` to `configured`, so a `go test`/`unittest`/wrapper command always fails and the check is permanently disabled). The function needs to distinguish "id genuinely absent" from "runner/collection failed", not treat both as absent.

chunk_findings.detail: The expanded default list is over-broad in a way that defeats the very guard it is meant to refine. `test_file_globs` is used to decide that a bug fix "changed only test files", which lets ddflow skip the requirement that the regression test actually fail on the pre-fix tree (per the knob's own doc: it then falls back to "the base's own test files, or ... the mutation given with the close"). The new patterns `spec/**`, `**/spec/**`, `**/*.spec.*` and `**/*_test.*` do not distinguish test specs/tests from ordinary non-test files that merely live under a `spec`/`specs` directory or carry a `.spec.`/`_spec.`/`.test.` infix. Concretely: a bug whose fix touches only `spec/architecture.md` (a design document), `api/openapi.spec.yaml` (an OpenAPI specification), or `contracts/petstore.spec.json` now matches `**/spec/**` / `**/*.spec.*` and will be classified as a "test-only" fix. ddflow will then not require the regression test to fail pre-fix and will accept the base's existing tests or a mutation instead — exactly the bypass that bug Bc262739f62 exists to prevent. The same holds for `**/*_test.*` matching non-test artifacts such as `load_test.md` or `aws_test.json`. Narrowing these to the conventions actually named in the doc (e.g. `**/*.test.js|ts|tsx|jsx`, `**/*_spec.rb`, `**/*_test.go`) or requiring a test-ish directory/file suffix would avoid misclassifying non-test changes as test-only.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lessons.py:53 (test_file_globs default)

chunk_findings.detail:
The two new infix patterns `**/*.test.*` and `**/*.spec.*` match any path containing a `.test.` or `.spec.` segment, with an unrestricted trailing extension — not just test sources. Concrete inputs that now satisfy the "regression test present" check without being tests at all:

- `**/*.test.*` matches environment/config artifacts such as `config/application.test.yml`, `docker-compose.test.yml`, `settings.test.json`, `values.test.yaml`. A fix that only edits the test-environment config is now classified as a test-only change.
- `**/*.spec.*` matches specification documents and contracts such as `docs/api.spec.md`, `openapi.spec.yaml`, `schema.spec.json`. A docs/contract-only edit is likewise classified as a test-only change.

Since these globs feed exactly the gate that bug Bc262739f62 uses to decide whether a test-only fix is acceptable, the over-match reverses the failure mode of this bug: instead of a real test tree being *rejected*, a non-test file is now *accepted* as the regression test, and a fix that changes no test at all can pass the requirement. The narrower patterns already in the list (`**/*_test.py`, `**/*_test.*`, `**/*_spec.*`, `**/tests/**`, `**/test/**`, `**/spec/**`, `**/__tests__/**`) cover the intended layouts; the bare `.test.`/`.spec.` infix (or at least constraining the extension to code/test-runner extensions, e.g. `*.test.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,mjs,cjs}` / `*.spec.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,rb,py}`) would avoid the false positives.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1433 (lessons.test_file_globs default)

chunk_findings.detail: The widened default is extension-agnostic for every test-naming convention *except* the `test_<name>` prefix, which is still pinned to Python (`"**/test_*.py"`) even though its new neighbours `"**/*_test.*"`, `"**/*.spec.*"`, `"**/*.test.*"` and `"**/*_spec.*"` all match any extension, and even though the project's own definition of a test file elsewhere in this very transcript (`enforce.readme_with_code`: "test_*.*, *_test.*, *_spec.*, *.test.*, *.spec.*") treats `test_*.*` as a test file for any extension. The bug this change closes is precisely "test_file_globs defaults cover only Python layouts", so a repo that uses the `test_<name>.<ext>` convention outside a `tests/`/`test/` directory — e.g. a Minitest-style project with `src/test_engine.rb`, or a JS project with `lib/test_widget.js` — is still not recognised: a fix whose only change is that file matches none of the globs, so `ddflow complete --regression-test` keeps refusing / takes the non-test path exactly as before Bbdd33740d6. Adding `"**/test_*.*"` (or replacing `"**/test_*.py"` with it) would close the remaining case; the `tests/**`/`test/**` entries only cover the subset that lives inside a test directory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (lessons.test_file_globs)

chunk_findings.detail: The broadened default adds a nested (`**/<dir>/**`) variant for every test directory it lists — `tests/**` + `**/tests/**`, `test/**` + `**/test/**`, `spec/**` + `**/spec/**`, `__tests__/**` + `**/__tests__/**` — but for `specs/**` only the root-anchored form is present; there is no `**/specs/**`. A directory named `specs` at any depth below the repo root is therefore not matched, and neither is `**/spec/**` (the path component must be exactly `spec`, not `specs`). The suffix patterns do not close the gap: they only match files whose name carries the convention (`*_spec.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*_test.*`, `*.test.*`, `test_*.*`), so a change touching only a non-suffixed file in a nested specs tree — a test helper/support file such as `services/api/specs/spec_helper.rb` or `packages/web/specs/fixtures/state.json` — matches nothing in this list. Closing the bug that fixes such a helper (`ddflow complete fix-… --regression-test …`) then hits exactly the failure Bbdd33740d6 describes: the check still treats the change as non-test-only and refuses, because the default is again too narrow for a non-Python layout. Adding `**/specs/**` (or dropping the redundant root-level forms if `**/` is treated as matching zero directories) would make `specs/` consistent with the other four directory families the same list enumerates.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1451 (`lessons.test_file_globs`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new default adds extension-agnostic name globs `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/*_test.*` and `**/*_spec.*`. Because the middle segments are `.*` (any extension), these do not only match test sources (`*.test.ts`, `*_spec.rb`, `foo_test.go`); they also match non-test artifacts that merely carry `.spec.`/`.test.`/`_spec.`/`_test.` in the name — e.g. an OpenAPI/schema document `api.spec.yaml`, `schemas/order.spec.json`, a note `docs/db-migration_test.md`, or a tooling file `tsconfig.spec.json`. The documented semantics of this knob are "when a bug's fix changes ONLY files matching these, the regression check cannot expect the test to fail on a pre-fix tree (the fix is in the test file itself)", so with this default a bug whose entire fix is confined to, say, `apischema/api.spec.yaml` is now classified as a test-only change: ddflow will run the base's own test files instead of requiring a regression test that fails on the unfixed tree, and `lessons.require_regression_test` / Bc262739f62 can be satisfied with no test actually covering the fix. Restricting these patterns to test-source extensions (`*.test.ts`/`*.spec.js`/`*_spec.rb`/`*_test.go`-style) or to test directories would avoid the false positives.

chunk_findings.detail: The widened default treats a top-level `specs/` tree as test files but not a nested one, so the very fix this change is for still misses a non-Python test layout. Path globs here are path globs in git pathspec form (`*` stops at `/`, `**/` is any depth — the convention stated for `[enforce].doc_globs` in the same output), so `specs/**` only matches a `specs/` directory at the repository root, while `**/specs/**` — present for `tests`, `test`, `spec` and `__tests__` but absent for `specs` — would be needed for `packages/api/specs/...`. Concretely: a bug whose regression test lives in `packages/web/specs/support/helpers.js` or `packages/api/specs/spec_helper.rb` (a file inside a nested spec tree that carries no `_spec`/`.spec` suffix, so the filename patterns `**/*_spec.*` / `**/*.spec.*` do not catch it either) is still not matched by any glob. The file is therefore treated as production code, `complete`/`ddflow complete fix-<bug> --regression-test <test>` demands the named test fail on the pre-fix tree, and the close is refused — exactly the Bc262739f62 refusal this change exists to remove, just in a monorepo layout (`packages/*/specs/`) rather than the flat one. Adding `'**/specs/**'` alongside `'specs/**'`, as was done for the three sibling directory names, closes the gap.

regression._collected via gates.tree_provides(scan=False)

chunk_findings.detail: The new probe answers "does pytest collect this?" with `tree_provides(..., scan=False)`, and `tree_provides` itself documents the state that makes this wrong: "OR it timed out or has no runner -- and the text scan decides" (ddflow/services/gates/regression_collect.py:56). With `scan=False` that decision is short-circuited to `False`, and there is no other fallback left: by the time `_collected` runs, the AST check (`_defines`) has already failed, which is precisely why the entry reached this branch. So in any environment where the configured runner cannot produce collect-only exit 0 — no `unit_tests` gate (`defn is None` → `configured = ""`), no pytest/deps on the host, a timeout, or an import failure in every candidate tree — `_collected` returns `False` and the entry is appended to `missing`, exactly as before the fix. Concretely, running `ddflow bug fixed Ba6c8cdeda4 --regression-test tests/test_v.py::test_v` on such a host for a `tests/test_v.py` containing `from helper import test_v` still reports the real, collectable test as existing in no worktree; the entry is even classified as `missing` rather than the `unchecked`/could-not-verify bucket, so the caller cannot tell "probe unavailable" from "test absent". The change only fixes the reported bug when the `unit_tests` gate exists, its command is pytest-based, and pytest actually succeeds in some tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/regression.py:_collected (`_collected` → `tree_provides(..., scan=False)`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_collected` is only reached after `_defines` — the AST def/class scan — has already failed in every tree, so there is no remaining "strict scan" for the docstring's justification to point at; `scan=False` throws away the only fallback that can see an imported binding. Concretely, in the environment this bug is about (a worktree created with `git worktree add`, where untracked dependencies like `.venv`, installed packages or the helper module are absent), the `unit_tests` gate command (e.g. `.venv/bin/pytest …`) cannot run: `run_command_gate(probe, root)[0]` is not `"passed"`, so `tree_provides` returns `scan and _scan(root, tests)` → `False`. For the reported case — `tests/test_v.py` containing `from helper import test_v` — `_unresolved_tests` therefore still appends `tests/test_v.py::test_v` to `missing` and `ddflow bug fixed` still refuses the real test, i.e. Ba6c8cdeda4 is only fixed when pytest happens to be runnable in one of the trees. The restored-test check uses the *whole* `tree_provides` (including `_scan`, B9f3ae012b9) precisely for this situation, and `_scan` here would find `test_v` in the file text; either `scan=True` or a module-level import/assignment binding scan (the other option the intent names) is needed for the fallback not to fail closed on the case it was added for.
